newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Chilean led group buys Argentine bank BUCI.
newsitem.headline: Chilean led group buys Argentine bank BUCI.

text.p: Corp Banca SA, controlled by Chilean financial group Infisa, won a tender to buy failed Argentine bank Banco Union Comercial e Industrial (BUCI), Argentina's Central Bank said.
"The agreement with Corp Banca gurantees BUCI's 80,000 savers will get back their $296 million in total deposits," the Central Bank added in a press release dated Sunday.
The deal entails a $118 million contribution from a banking security net and the issuing of $30 million in subordinated corporate bonds by a banking capitalization trustee fund, it said.
BUCI has 48 branches and had requested permission to open another five when it ran into financial trouble.
The Central Bank took control of the bank last August at BUCI's request when it had almost $300 million in deposits, $334 million in loans and a net worth of $10.3 million.
